newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WELSH PAIR TO STAKE TEST CLAIMS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELSH PAIR TO STAKE TEST CLAIMS.

text.p: Welsh centres Scott Gibbs and Allan Bateman have the chance to overtake their English rivals in the race for a Lions test place in the second match of their South African tour against Border on Wednesday.

Gibbs and Bateman watched from the touchlines on Saturday as England's Jeremy Guscott and uncapped Leicester centre Will Greenwood ran in three tries between them in the Lions' opening day 39-11 victory over an Eastern Province Invitation XV.
"Everyone agrees that Will had a tremendous game and Jerry is on fire at the moment -- even in training," said Gibbs.
"Every position in the team is up for grabs still but they certainly put in a great performance."

The pairing of Guscott's rapier with Greenwood's broadsword was one of the highlights of Saturday's match. Many South African commentators were baffled as to how they could have been kept out of England's Five Nations team by Phil de Glanville and Will Carling.
Scottish centre Alan Tait has to wait until Saturday's match against Western Province for his first chance.
"There is a general respect among the five of us but the element of competition is definitely there," added Gibbs.
"That's a healthy thing and none of us are under any illusions about how tough it is going to be to get a test place."
Bateman said: "I enjoy playing with Scott and hopefully we can stake our claim to a test place."
Gibbs was due to partner Guscott last Saturday in the predicted test pairing but was forced to withdraw with illness.
He and Bateman, as well as Tait, returned to rugby union from rugby league this season and are joined by two other returnees in the side to meet Border.
Wales and former St Helen's prop David Young is on the tighthead while John Bentley, who last played international rugby union for England in 1988, is on the wing.

Test skipper Martin Johnson is rested again and will make his first appearance on Saturday as the tour gathers intensity with a match against South Africa's new Nite Series champions Western Province at Newlands in Cape Town, venue of the first est.
Flanker Tim Rodber, who missed Saturday's match through illness, required five stitches in a gash on his forehead during training on Monday and again takes no part.
The other four tourists yet to start a match are Tait, hooker Barry Williams, scrumhalf Matt Dawson and prop Paul Wallace.
Border, who won only two of their Nite Series games, name a young side captained by Springbok squad member, full-back Russell Bennett.

Border - 15-Russell Bennett (captain; 14-Kelly Hilton-Green, 13-Greg Hechter, 12-Kaya Malotana, 11-Andre Classen; 10-Greg Miller, 9-John Bradbrook; 8-Andre Fox, 7-Anton Botha, 6-Marius Swart, 5-Johan Gehring, 4-Streicher Botha, 3-Delarey du Preez, 2-Ruhan van Zyl, 1-Heinrich Kok.

Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Scott Gibbs, 12-Alan Bateman, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Paul Grayson, 9-Austin Healey; 8-Eric Millar, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright (captain), 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Doddie Weir, 3-David Young, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.
